back: System software that manages hardware and software resources, provides an interface and provides a platform for applications.
Managing files, memory, peripherals and drivers, multitasking, interrupts, user accounts and security; providing an interface and a platform for applications.
Allocating RAM to each program, freeing it when the program closes, preventing programs overwriting each other, using virtual memory when RAM is full.
Running several programs apparently at once by sharing processor time (rapid switching) and memory between them.
The OS communicates with devices through device drivers, detects new devices (plug and play) and queues jobs such as printing.
GUI: windows, icons, menus, pointer; easy to learn, more resources. CLI: typed commands; efficient and powerful, but commands must be learned.
Mobile: touch, app store, strict battery and memory management, built-in GPS and mobile data. PC: mouse and keyboard, many windows, large programs, many peripherals.

front: Why do applications need an OS?
back: They request services (files, memory, printing) from the OS instead of controlling the hardware themselves; the OS is their platform.
